title: Conversation Mosaic: KV coalescer for microbatch prefix dedup and GPU slab compaction
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Introduce a lightweight coalescer that observes short-window conversation fragments across concurrent requests and produces a compacted, content-addressed prefix artifact (the 'mosaic') that can be reused across microbatches. The mosaic should reduce redundant KV residency on GPU and enable slab compaction without increasing tail latency for single-request hot paths.
background: We currently waste GPU KV memory when multiple concurrent requests share overlapping prompt prefixes or repeated template sections. Existing heuristics either dedupe aggressively (risking hash collisions and mis-shares) or conservatively (leaving redundant slabs). Users with chatty workloads and high interleaving see 10-35% higher GPU occupancy and increased OOM incidents during peak multi-tenant bursts.
success_metrics: Reduce average GPU KV slab occupancy per-instance by >=20% for interleaved chat workloads
Lower OOM intervention incidents in staging by 50% during 95th-percentile QPS spikes
Maintain 95th-percentile single-request decode latency within 5% of baseline
Decrease token-level serving cost for sample benchmark set by >=12%
design_decisions: Use a content-addressed fragment ID (sha1 trimmed to 64 bits) combined with sequence metadata to identify mosaic candidates
Operate coalescer as a non-blocking observer in the request path: candidates are published to the mosaic store asynchronously to avoid tail-latency regression
Limit mosaic formation window to 200ms per slab-slot to bound reordering and memory churn
Prefer exact substring matches for coalescing over similarity heuristics in the first iteration to minimize false-positive sharing
Provide a lightweight eviction hint that allows the slab allocator to prioritize mosaic-backed fragments for compaction when GPU pressure exceeds soft threshold
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (POC): implement observer hooks at the batching ingress to extract prefix fragments and compute fragment IDs (ENG-762341-1)
Phase 2: implement in-memory mosaic registry and async publisher that writes compacted fragment entries to the content-addressed shard store (ENG-762341-2)
Phase 3: integrate mosaic hints with slab allocator; allow slab compaction to reclaim redundant ranges referenced only by mosaic artifacts (ENG-762341-3)
Phase 4: add safe-guard: validate reuse at decode-time by checking fragment checksum to avoid silent corruption
Phase 5: telemetry and dashboarding; add per-instance mosaic hit/miss, garbage collection rate, and latency heatmaps
acceptance_criteria: Mosaic registry integrates without adding >2ms median to request ingress path (observer path must be async)
Mosaic-backed slab compaction results in >=15% median reduction in GPU KV memory for the benchmark profile
No production-facing correctness regressions in prompt outputs across 10k example prompts (fuzzed) after reuse
Feature can be toggled via runtime flag and rolled back without allocator restart
testing_plan: Unit: fragment ID generation, checksum verification, and registry operations
Integration: deploy to staging fleet with synthetic interleaved chat workload (mix of pinned prompts + generated noise) to measure occupancy and latency
Chaos: simulate slab eviction and forced OOM to verify safe rollback and recovery
Canary: 5% traffic on dedicated cluster with runtime-1.22 and monitor Mosaic hit rate, tail latency, and correctness metrics for 48h
rollout_strategy: Feature gated behind runtime flag and telemetry opt-in
Start with read-only mosaic observation (collect candidate stats) for 2 weeks
Enable async publish and GC in staging; validate memory improvements
Enable slab compaction hints in a limited canary (5% traffic) and monitor for correctness and tail-latency
Gradual ramp to 100% if telemetry passes for 72h
